title: Restoration Software: Tools for Jobs, Drying Logs and Claims
html:
Restoration software starts with one platform for job files, photos and drying records. Pick a restoration tool such as Albiware or Encircle, add a photo app and your accounting app, then build a website that wins emergency calls. Published prices in this guide run from $29 to $583 a month, and some vendors do not publish a price at all.

Restoration software has to prove the work, not only schedule it. A water loss file needs dated photos, moisture readings, drying logs and a scope that an insurance adjuster will accept. A tool built for a lawn crew does not hold that file together, so the first question is what each product records.

This guide sorts restoration tools by the job they do: mitigation documentation, photo proof, general job management, rebuild project control and accounting. Each tool gets the price its own vendor shows and one real limit.

Which restoration software holds the job file together?

Albiware and Encircle are the two products built around the restoration job file. Both sit between the field crew and the office, and both aim at water, fire and mold losses.

  • Albiware: its site lists restoration job management, drying logs, field documentation, floor plans, a CRM and built-in payments. Fit: a restoration company that wants one system from first call to final invoice. Limit: its prices are not public. Ask the vendor for a quote.
  • Encircle: covers field documentation, floor plans, moisture and drying records, contents inventory and a scope to estimate step that exports to Xactimate. Field documentation lists at $285 a month, and field documentation with scope to estimate lists at $583 a month, both on monthly billing. Limit: plans run on a 12-month term and are priced by yearly job volume. The page does not say which volume tier the listed price covers.

The two products overlap, but they start from different places. Encircle begins with documentation in the field and adds estimating on top. Albiware presents itself as a full job management system. Ask each for a demo using one of your own recent losses so you see how a real file looks.

A short test helps. Take a water loss from last quarter and list what the adjuster asked for. If the answer was photos, moisture readings, a floor plan and a scope, check that the tool produces all four without exports to other apps.

Which tool keeps photo proof organized on every loss?

CompanyCam is a photo and project documentation app that crews can run on a phone. It does one job well: it ties timestamped photos to a project so the office never hunts for pictures.

  • CompanyCam: Core is $63 a month billed annually, Crew is $129 a month and Scale is $199 a month, with additional users at $29 each. Crew adds checklists, task assignment and live job tracking. Fit: a crew that already has a job system and needs better field proof. Limit: Core includes one user and caps at two, and a monthly price is not listed.

A photo app does not replace drying logs or a scope. It does make a good second tool when the main system is a general job manager. A restoration company with two or three project managers can run CompanyCam on Crew and keep the rest in a simple system.

Storage and sharing deserve a question too. Ask whether adjusters, homeowners and subcontractors can view a project without paying for a seat. Each extra seat at $29 a month adds up across a crew of ten.

Photo habits matter more than the app. Shoot every room before work starts, after demolition, during drying and at completion. Name each shot by room and date. A tool only keeps what the crew captures.

Can general job management software run a restoration company?

Jobber and Housecall Pro can run a small restoration or repair crew, but only for the scheduling, quoting and invoicing side. They are priced for trade businesses at large.

  • Jobber: the Core plan is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually, for one user. Connect and Grow plans add features and users, and extra users cost $29 a month each. Limit: card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents, and large insurance payments feel that fee.
  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually or $79 monthly for one user. Essentials is $149 or $189 for five users. Max is $299 or $329 for eight users. Limit: Max charges $35 a month per user beyond eight, and many add-ons show no price.

These fit best for reconstruction and repair work after the mitigation job is closed.

Do not buy a general tool and a restoration tool for the same crew on day one. Pick the file system that matches your largest line of work, then add the second only when a gap costs you money.

Which software controls rebuild projects and the books?

Restoration firms that also rebuild need project cost control and clean accounting. Two project tools and one accounting package cover most of that.

Restoration cash flow has its own pattern: large invoices, insurance payers and progress billing. Whatever you choose, test that it can split one loss into mitigation and rebuild invoices without double entry.

Which free and paid tools bring emergency calls in?

Software runs the work, but calls come from search, maps and ads. Google states that creating a Business Profile is free, and a complete profile is the first lead tool a restoration company should own.

Limit: a profile alone will not win a competitive market. Restoration searches are urgent, so rankings and ads decide who gets the call.

Paid search matters for emergency work because homeowners search at the moment of loss. See the pricing page for the full list.

What should you ask in a restoration software demo?

Ask for a demo on one of your own closed losses, not the vendor's sample file. A clean sample hides the problems that show up in real work.

  • Records: can the app show photos, moisture readings, equipment placed and a floor plan in one report for the adjuster?
  • Offline use: does the field app keep working in a basement or a building with no signal, and does it sync later?
  • Export: which formats leave the system, and can you take your data with you if you cancel?
  • Contract: how long is the term, what happens to price when job volume grows, and what does onboarding cost?
  • People: how many users are included, and does a subcontractor or an adjuster need a paid seat to view a file?

Write the answers in a simple sheet and score each vendor the same way. A product with a lower price and a missing export costs more once an adjuster asks for a report in the wrong format.

Plan the rollout before you sign. Pick one project manager as the owner, load three live jobs first, and keep the old process running for a short overlap. Adoption fails when the field crew sees the app as extra work, so ask crew leads what slows them down before you pick the tool.

How do you choose restoration software for your company?

Choose restoration software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you sign.

Cost: add the plan, extra users, job-volume tiers, add-ons and card fees. Ask what happens at the end of a 12-month term.

Setup effort: can a project manager learn the field app in one week, and can the office import current jobs without paying for data entry?

A small crew handling a few losses a month can run CompanyCam on Core, QuickBooks Simple Start and a Jobber Core plan. That stack stays under a few hundred dollars a month on published prices. It lacks drying logs, so confirm your carriers accept photo-based records first.

A multi-crew company handling a steady flow of insurance work fits Albiware or Encircle. Add JobTread or Contractor Foreman only when rebuild budgets need their own system. Budget for vendor onboarding time, since the cost of a restoration platform shows up in the first month of rollout.

Company sizeStarting stackAdd next
Small crew, few losses a monthCompanyCam Core, QuickBooks, Jobber CoreMitigation file system
Growing, insurance heavyAlbiware or Encircle, QuickBooksCompanyCam for extra crews
Mitigation plus rebuildRestoration platform plus JobTread or Contractor ForemanMarketing support for lead flow

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. For more ideas, see these restoration marketing ideas .

How much does restoration software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from $29 a month for Jobber Core billed annually to $583 a month for Encircle with scope to estimate. Albiware does not show a price on its page. Card fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so confirm totals with each vendor.

Does restoration software include drying logs?

Restoration-specific products do. Albiware lists drying logs in its product menu, and Encircle lists moisture and drying records. General tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro focus on scheduling, quotes and invoices, so confirm drying features before you rely on them.

Can a small restoration company use Jobber?

Yes, for scheduling, quoting and invoicing. Jobber Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 a month billed annually for one user. It will not replace a restoration documentation system, so pair it with a photo tool and confirm carrier requirements.

Do restoration companies need a website if they use job software?

Yes. Job software runs the work after the phone rings, but it does not bring calls in. A website with pages for water, fire and mold services, plus a verified Google Business Profile, gives homeowners a reason to call you first.

Is CompanyCam enough for restoration photo documentation?

It handles photos, checklists and reports well, but it does not replace drying logs or a scope. CompanyCam Core is $63 a month billed annually and caps at two users. Use it beside a restoration platform or a general job tool, not instead of one.

What should a new restoration company buy first?

Start with a photo tool, accounting software and a free Google Business Profile. Add a restoration file system when losses grow and adjusters ask for more records. Buy rebuild project software only when you carry rebuild budgets and change orders.
